title: Summer crop season closes with below-average yield prospects
france: Northern Spain, France, Benelux countries, southern Germany, Italy, Austria, Czechia, Slovakia, Hungary, Slovenia, Croatia, western Romania and parts of Ukraine: Impacts documented in earlier editions of the bulletin persisted through the end of the season across large parts of western, central and south-eastern Europe. September rainfall offered some relief but arrived too late to reverse earlier yield losses. In several of these regions (e.g. France, southern Germany, Austria, Slovakia, Slovenia and Croatia) crops further deteriorated in September owing to insufficient soil moisture.

title: Heatwaves impact summer and winter crops

Favourable crop conditions across Europe, with emerging water deficits
Crops exit from winter dormancy in favourable conditions
Winter crops fare well despite cold and wet episodes
france: Winter crop conditions across Europe remain broadly satisfactory, although recent extreme weather has increased regional contrasts. Severe and persistent frost in parts of northern and eastern Europe has heightened concerns about local frost damage, particularly where snow cover was insufficient at the onset of cold spells. Winter wheat is generally well hardened, but more sensitive crops may have been adversely affected. In contrast, abundant rainfall in parts of western France, southern Europe and the western Mediterranean region has replenished soil moisture reserves, but with localised flooding. The main area of concern relates to severe frost affecting northern and eastern Europe. Secondary concerns arise from excessive rainfall in parts of western France, south-western Europe and the western Maghreb. Frost events affecting northern and eastern Europe

title: Disappointing summer crop season in the south-east
france: Sowing and early establishment of winter crops progressing well at large, by Stefan Niemeyer In short The 2025 summer crop harvest is under way, with mostly near or above-average summer crop yields expected at EU level. Only grain maize and sunflower have been strongly affected in the south-eastern Europe, pulling the EU outlook down to –3 % and –10 % below the five-year average, respectively. In contrast, near- or above-average yields for most summer crops are forecast in northern and western European countries. This October edition of the JRC MARS Bulletin includes an extended section on sowing conditions and the early establishment of winter crops across Europe. Favourable weather and field conditions from France to Poland, and from Scandinavia to Italy, have supported timely sowing with good emergence and early crop development. In contrast, excessive wetness in parts of Bulgaria and Romania delayed winter cereal sowings, while in Portugal, Spain and parts of eastern Croatia and Hungary the sowing of winter crops has been delayed due to continuously dry soils. Uniform crop emergence in these regions will require rainfall arriving soon that, indeed, is likely to occur in the coming weeks. The summer crop season is coming to an end with no new impacts recorded and only minor concerns identified for the beginning of the new winter crop season.

title: Summer drought reduces yields in south-east Europe
france: Overall prospects for rice are positive, with Italy, Spain, Portugal and France showing strong yield potential, whereas southern Spain, Bulgaria, Romania and Greece face a mediocre to poor outlook. The overall EU rice yield is forecast to reach 6 % above the five-year average.
